newsitem.title: USA: NY State Electric seeks state tax change.
newsitem.headline: NY State Electric seeks state tax change.

text.p: New York State Electric & Gas Corp customers would have saved $48 million last year if New York state had taxed utilities on their profits instead of their gross revenues, the company said Tuesday, releasing testimony submitted February 21 to the Senate Finance and Assembly Ways and Means committees.

"Our customers paid $83 million in state gross receipts tax (GRT) in 1996. If our taxes were based on net income as they are for other corporations our customers would have paid $35 million, a savings of $48 million," chief financial officer
Sherwood J. Rafferty told the legislators.
"In 1996, the Senate passed legislation to phase out the GRT, but the Assembly did not. In 1997, we urge the Senate and Assembly to phase out the GRT as soon as possible," he said.

The benefit of the phase-out of this tax on all utility revenues would be immediately passed on to utility customers, NYSEG pointed out. As a result, utility customers across the state would benefit from GRT relief.

This legislative session presents an especially good time to deal with the GRT because of the $50 million Governor Pataki has allocated in his executive budget for a job-creating tax cut to be developed with the legislature, the utility pointed out.
In 1996, it said, $0.19 of every dollar NYSEG received from retail electric customers was used to pay taxes totaling $296 million. And that does not include sales taxes.
"Since 1988 our costs have remained relatively flat. During the same time our tax bill and the excessive, government-imposed cost of nonutility generation, together, have tripled, Rafferty said.
"We will continue to control our costs, but the external pressures that are driving up electricity prices must also be addressed," he said. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
